scores.evidence: The lesson uses warm です・ます throughout, with no banned phrases (lint --strict is clean), and it reads naturally, e.g. s1-b5 「答えを出してもらうのではなく、考えを引き出してもらうと、作りたいものがはっきりします。」. Some small slips remain. The round-3 分かる→わかる pass missed 「分かれば」 twice in check-quiz q1. hook-predict feedback mixes 「足りなかった」 and 「足りない」.

Lint reports no sentence-length or paragraph-length findings. Each segment brings in at most 2–3 terms (s5-defs: MVP, MoSCoW; s3-defs: 1枚企画書, PRD). Every section has a table, diagram, steps or quiz. The body is still above the length budget the brief records, so this is not a 4.

The lesson lists ch0 and ch1 as prerequisites and recalls them in s1-b1 (「第0章で、人間の仕事は…」) and s3-steps (「第1章で見たデータベース」). Every term is defined before use and matches the glossary, e.g. 目的 in s2-defs and glossary[1]. The abbreviations MVP and PRD are spelled out in full.

Both locales are complete, including the mermaid labels, alt text, prompt variables and checklist. The EN is natural and matches the JP meaning, and the practice-tip label 「期待される結果」 matches the PromptBlock UI. The s2-b4 description paraphrases the screen label (「残り金額が変わった画面」). The EN also renders 通知 two ways: "notification" in 2-2 and "reminder" elsewhere.

mustFix.issue: q1 option b feedback still writes 「分かれば」 in kanji. The round-3 pass changed 分かる to わかる everywhere else, and the style guide and ch1 use わかる.
mustFix.fix: 「目的が分かれば、カレンダー以外の手段が合うこともあります。」→「目的がわかれば、カレンダー以外の手段が合うこともあります。」

mustFix.issue: The q1 explanation has the same 「分かれば」 left over.
mustFix.fix: 「「予定の重なりにすぐ気づきたい」と分かれば、ほかの手段も選べます。」→「「予定の重なりにすぐ気づきたい」とわかれば、ほかの手段も選べます。」

mustFix.issue: This feedback uses present tense, but the option a feedback for the same question uses past tense (「足りなかったのは」). Both talk about the same past request, so the tense should match.
mustFix.fix: options[1].feedback.jp 「AIを替えても、自分の困りごとは伝わりません。足りないのは性能ではなく、目的の情報です。」→「AIを替えても、自分の困りごとは伝わりません。足りなかったのは性能ではなく、目的の情報です。」

mustFix.issue: The description calls the screen 「残り金額が変わった画面」. The diagram label, alt text and s3-steps all call it 「今月の残り画面」. Screen-reader users should hear the same label.
mustFix.fix: description.jp 「支出を入力して保存すると、残り金額が変わった画面に戻ります。」→「支出を入力して保存すると、今月の残り画面に戻ります。残り金額は新しい額に変わっています。」 (EN can stay: "Log an expense and save it, and you're back on the money-left screen with the new amount.")

niceToHave: s3-check explanation: Claude Code has not appeared in ch0 or ch1, and the round-3 edit removed its gloss. Consider a short gloss again, e.g. 「AIツールのClaude Codeの公式ガイドも、…」. Also, 「よい仕様書…の条件として」 states the source more strongly than it says ("The most useful specs … state what is out of scope"). 「特徴として」 would be closer.
s2-table row 2, goal cell: 「入力忘れによる記録の抜けを防げる」 → 「入力を忘れて記録が抜けるのを防げる」 reads more easily. Check the 390px width again if you change it.
EN consistency: 通知 is "notification" in s2-b1, s2-defs and s2-check, but "reminder" elsewhere. Use one word, probably "reminder", in every place.
EN spelling register: s2-check uses British "rota" while hook-predict uses American "color". Consider "schedule" / "duty schedule".
Step `expect` texts in s3-steps and practice-steps end in plain form (「1文ができる。」「並ぶ。」) while prompt-block `expect` texts use です・ます. Record the convention in the style guide or switch to ます形.
s2-check: only the correct option (c) is phrased as 「〜できる」; check whether the form gives the answer away.
s1-b1: 「ビジョン」 appears without English; check whether ch0 already glossed it.
summary: The Japanese reads like a patient teacher: short sentences, one idea per paragraph, and terms used consistently across the text, tables, the diagram and the glossary. The EN is complete and natural. Four small fixes remain: two leftover 「分かれば」 in check-quiz q1, a tense mismatch in the hook-predict feedback, and the s2-b4 diagram description, which should use the label 「今月の残り画面」.
